context: The employer withheld gratuity alleging misconduct. Whether gratuity can be forfeited absent proof of loss. Following Ramesh Traders v. Kavita Builders, [1963] 3 SCR 515, actual loss must be shown before forfeiture. The withholding is set aside.

The buyer defaulted on payment under an agreement to sell. Whether the earnest money clause permits forfeiture of the full deposit. The ratio in Ramesh Traders v. Kavita Builders, [1963] 3 SCR 515 is distinguishable as the deposit here was nominal. The appeal is dismissed.

The tenant paid an advance which the landlord retained. Whether retention of advance requires proof of damage. Relying on Ramesh Traders v. Kavita Builders, [1963] 3 SCR 515, the landlord must prove loss. The petition is allowed.

The contractor's security deposit was encashed. Whether liquidated damages require proof of actual loss. We follow the principle in Ramesh Traders v. Kavita Builders, [1963] 3 SCR 515. The appeal is allowed.

The levy was challenged as lacking any service in return. Whether Sunder Lal v. State of Mysore lays down the correct law. Sunder Lal v. State of Mysore, [1971] 2 SCR 40 is overruled; a fee need not be matched by a specific service. The appeal is allowed.
